newsitem.title: UK: Russian palladium exports soar in 1996 - CRU.
newsitem.headline: Russian palladium exports soar in 1996 - CRU.

text.p: Deliveries of palladium from Russia to the United States and Switzerland soared late last year, according to data from CRU International.
Quoting customs statistics, CRU said the absence of Russian shipments to Japan contrasted starkly with U.S. imports which doubled their normal level in October and then rose again in November.
"(The November figure) reached 23,457 kgs, equivalent to a quarter of all U.S. imports of palladium in 1995 and more than double the total for any previous month," CRU said in monthly report.
"In January-November, the USA imported no less than 58.5 tonnes of Russian palladium, an increase of 77 percent," it noted.
Palladium was fixed at a fresh six-month high of $130.50 per ounce on Friday reflecting consumer and speculative buying in an increasingly tight spot market.
Earlier this week dealers said the premium over ingot for sponge grade material -- the grade most commonly used by U.S. autocatalyst makers -- was over $3.00 per ounce.
Possible reasons for the higher shipments, according to CRU, were "a window of opportunity" opening before the old sales structure was dismantled and a new one put in its place.
Alternatively the authorites may have anticipated delays and reshipped metal to cover first quarter sales to the U.S. market, it said.
Swiss deliveries were up 72 percent to 26.7 tonnes in the year to December.
"Thus despite a 21 percent fall in exports to Japan last year, overall Russian deliveries to its main western markets in January-November rose no less than 23 percent to 130.80 tonnes," CRU said.
"Whatever the explanation for these developments, the implication is that Riussian palladium stocks remain very large," it said.
Platinum deliveries from Russia in contrast fell 25.5 percent to the main westrer marketrs last year to 31.135 tonnes, according to CRU quoting customs statistics.
U.S. deliveries were up 14.1 percent lastyear to 5.114 tonnes but Swiss imports were down 66 percent to 4.179 tonnes and Japanese deliveries fell 23.6 percent to 22.57 tonnes.
